sources.title: How to train your dog to focus on you

claims.statement: Dogs Trust focus training rewards the dog for voluntarily looking at the handler, building engagement before adding distractions.

Dogs Trust training pages consistently progress skills by reducing distraction and increasing difficulty gradually; KindTrail synthesises this as distance before duration before distraction for app progression (charity-aligned heuristic).
claims.excerptOrParaphrase: DDD heuristic aligned to charity gradual progression.
claims.confidenceJustification: Cross-page synthesis; not single explicit DDD article.
limitations: Human review for app tier thresholds.
See disc-006: Dogs Trust stay and target-training pages build duration before distance or distraction, which differs from the distance-first order synthesised here.

claims.statement: Blue Cross stress guidance (batch 002 source) lists lip licking, yawning, pinned ears, and turning away as stress signs owners should notice before escalation.

protocols.title: Distance → duration → distraction (KindTrail skeleton)
protocols.intendedOutcome: Owner increases one difficulty dimension at a time when proofing behaviours.

steps.instruction: Increase distance from dog while maintaining behaviour (e.g. sit/stay) before lengthening duration.
steps.progressCriteria: Success at new distance with 3 repetitions.

steps.instruction: Increase duration only after distance stable; then add mild distractions one at a time.
steps.rewardTiming: High-value rewards for first successes with distraction.
steps.progressCriteria: Behaviour holds with one new distraction type.
steps.easierIfStruggling: Return to previous D or D level.

protocols.generalisationMaintenance: Cycle through DDD for each new skill.
protocols.reviewReason: Synthesised DDD skeleton; tier numbers need validation.

behaviours.name: Owner recognises stress sign
behaviours.observableCriteria: Owner can name at least two stress signs (e.g. lip lick, yawning) when dog shows them and pauses training.

lessons.title: Read stress signals
lessons.summary: Notice lip licks, yawning, and turning away—pause and help your dog feel safe.
